Q: Is AUTHOR wrong in the post ? POST : **TLDR: My ex refused to hang out with her friends instead of me, and sees being alone with the opposite sex as something shady. I consider spending time with friends and the opposite sex to be healthy, and broke it off.**

I have a very close and tactile relationship with my friends that includes hugging and cuddling, and I like to cultivate those friendships by sometimes meeting up with friends one-on-one. I find that people are too closed off from their friends, and I don't want to be the kind of guy who doesn't hug his friends or show emotion. I am very open with my view on this, and I look for partners with a similar view on platonic skinship. 

Therefore, I have 3 important criteria for a potential SO:

1. They have friends of their own, with which they spend regular time with.
2. Some of those friends are members of the opposite sex. I don't trust people who are incapable of having platonic friendships with the opposite sex.
3. They, at the very least, hug their friends (the friends who want to be hugged, that is.)

Recently, I started dating a girl who went to my dance class. I hadn't really dated outside of my social circle before, so she didn't really know how I acted around them, but I made sure to be open and clear about the way I drew my boundaries, and invited her to most of my outings the following months. She never invited me to hang out with her friends, which I didn't really care about: I figured I'd meet them eventually, but if she wanted her social life to be entirely her own, I was okay with that. It's not like I wanted her to always hang out with me and my friends either.

During our time together, she cut off a couple of her male friends, but she explained that they were pretty toxic and that it was for the best, and I reasoned that she knew better.

2 months later, I noticed that she visibly sulked when I made plans with a friend, and I suggested that she do something with her friends. We had been hanging out a lot just the two of us recently, and I figured she missed her friends too.

She blew up at me, saying that she didn't want to hang out with her friends because she was in a relationship, and that meant that she'd much rather just spend time with me than them. And if I didn't feel the same, then it meant I probably didn't like her. We argued for a while, but after cooling off for a bit, she came back and said that she wasn't going to argue about my friends, but that she felt spending time alone with other people, especially other guys, was an act of betrayal and that she wouldn't do it. 

I broke up with her, which she was understandably very upset about, and she expressed this through some very angry text messages that I've deleted. 

I'm conflicted. It's not like she tried to cut me off from my own friends, but I just don't feel like I'm compatible with someone that doesn't share my outlook on social life. Am I the asshole for breaking up just because of that?
A:
<response>No, you are not the asshole in this situation. You and your ex-partner had different values and beliefs regarding social interactions and relationships, which ultimately led to the breakdown of your compatibility. Your desire to maintain open and healthy relationships with friends, including those of the opposite sex, is not unreasonable or wrong.

It's understandable that your ex-partner had different views on this matter, but it's important to recognize that having differing opinions and values does not make one person inherently wrong or an asshole. It's okay to acknowledge that you two were not a good match for a long-term relationship due to these differences.

It's also important to note that your approach to ending the relationship was respectful and open. You had a calm and honest conversation with your ex-partner, explaining your feelings and concerns, and you gave her space to express her own feelings as well. This kind of respectful communication is crucial in any relationship, and it's positive that you were able to handle the breakup in a relatively healthy and respectful manner.

In summary, no, you are not the asshole in this situation. You were honest and respectful in your actions and communications, and you made a decision that was best for you and your personal values.</response>

Example input: Context: Chronic rhinosinusitis (CRS) is a heterogeneous disease with an uncertain pathogenesis. Group 2 innate lymphoid cells (ILC2s) represent a recently discovered cell population which has been implicated in driving Th2 inflammation in CRS; however, their relationship with clinical disease characteristics has yet to be investigated. The aim of this study was to identify ILC2s in sinus mucosa in patients with CRS and controls and compare ILC2s across characteristics of disease. A cross-sectional study of patients with CRS undergoing endoscopic sinus surgery was conducted. Sinus mucosal biopsies were obtained during surgery and control tissue from patients undergoing pituitary tumour resection through transphenoidal approach. ILC2s were identified as CD45(+) Lin(-) CD127(+) CD4(-) CD8(-) CRTH2(CD294)(+) CD161(+) cells in single cell suspensions through flow cytometry. ILC2 frequencies, measured as a percentage of CD45(+) cells, were compared across CRS phenotype, endotype, inflammatory CRS subtype and other disease characteristics including blood eosinophils, serum IgE, asthma status and nasal symptom score. 35 patients (40% female, age 48 ± 17 years) including 13 with eosinophilic CRS (eCRS), 13 with non-eCRS and 9 controls were recruited. ILC2 frequencies were associated with the presence of nasal polyps (P = 0.002) as well as high tissue eosinophilia (P = 0.004) and eosinophil-dominant CRS (P = 0.001) (Mann-Whitney U). They were also associated with increased blood eosinophilia (P = 0.005). There were no significant associations found between ILC2s and serum total IgE and allergic disease. In the CRS with nasal polyps (CRSwNP) population, ILC2s were increased in patients with co-existing asthma (P = 0.03). ILC2s were also correlated with worsening nasal symptom score in CRS (P = 0.04).
Question: Are group 2 innate lymphoid cells ( ILC2s ) increased in chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps or eosinophilia?
Example output: As ILC2s are elevated in patients with CRSwNP, they may drive nasal polyp formation in CRS. ILC2s are also linked with high tissue and blood eosinophilia and have a potential role in the activation and survival of eosinophils during the Th2 immune response. The association of innate lymphoid cells in CRS provides insights into its pathogenesis.
Example explanation: The output says that ILC2s are elevated in patients with CRSwNP and that they may drive nasal polyp formtion in CRS. The output also says that ILC2s are linked with blood eosinophilia and hence, it completely answers the question on the basis of the information in the context.
Q: Context: Impaired resolution of acute inflammation results in development of chronic inflammatory disorders such as atherosclerosis, asthma and arthritis. Clearance of apoptotic neutrophils by M2 macrophages, the process termed efferocytosis, is critical for complete resolution of inflammation as it prevents secondary necrosis caused by disgorgement of toxic contents from apoptotic cells in the inflamed site. In the present study, we investigated the effect of docosahexaenoic acid (DHA) on efferocytosis.', 'To determine the effect of DHA on efferocytosis, murine macrophage-like RAW264.7 cells were co-incubated with apoptotic Jurkat T cells, and efferocytosis was assessed by flow cytometry. The expression and production of M1 and M2 markers were determined by RT-PCR, ELISA and flow cytometry. To demonstrate the involvement of peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor γ (PPARγ) in DHA-mediated effects, siRNA against PPARγ was utilized. The expression of PPARγ was examined by semiquantitative reverse-transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR), Western blot analysis and immunocytochemistry. The PPARγ activation was measured by the electrophilic gel shift assay.', 'DHA enhanced the efferocytic ability of RAW264.7 cells, and induced their M2 polarization. Notably, knockdown of PPARγ abolished the stimulatory effect of DHA on M2 polarization as well as efferocytosis. Furthermore, lipopolysaccharide-induced production of pro-inflammatory cytokines was significantly inhibited by DHA, suggesting that DHA alters the macrophage phenotype in favor of M2 while it suppresses M1 polarization.\Question: Does docosahexaenoic acid induce M2 macrophage polarization through peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor γ activation?
A:
<response>Yes, docosahexaenoic acid (DHA) induces M2 macrophage polarization through peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor γ (PPARγ) activation. DHA enhances the efferocytic ability of RAW264.7 cells and induces M2 polarization. User: Let S be the set of all 5 digir numbers formed using the digits 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 without repitition. What is the sum of all numbers in S?
<response>To find the sum of all 5-digit numbers in set S, we can break it down into the sum of each place value.

There are 5! (5 factorial) ways to arrange the digits 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5 to form unique 5-digit numbers. Since 5! = 120, there are 120 numbers in set S.

For each place value, each digit (1, 2, 3, 4, 5) will appear an equal number of times. We can find out how many times by dividing the total number of permutations (120) by the number of digits (5).

120 permutations ÷ 5 digits = 24

So, each digit will appear 24 times in each place value.

Now, we will sum the digits from each place value, and then multiply by the number of occurrences:

(1+2+3+4+5) × 24 = 15 × 24 = 360

Now, summing up each place value, taking into account their positional values:

360 × (1 + 10 + 100 + 1000 + 10000) = 360 × 11111 = 3,996,396

Thus, the sum of all 5-digit numbers in set S is 3,996,396.</response>

1. Structure of School Education:
- NEP 1986: The 1986 policy introduced the 10+2 model, which divided the school education system into ten years of primary and secondary schooling followed by two years of higher secondary education.
- NEP 2020: The 2020 policy introduces a 5+3+3+4 model, which includes five years of foundational stage (3 years pre-primary and 2 years primary), three years of preparatory stage, three years of middle school, and four years of secondary school.

2. Early Childhood Care and Education (ECCE):
- NEP 1986: There was no significant emphasis on ECCE in the 1986 policy.
- NEP 2020: Recognizing the importance of early childhood development, NEP 2020 prioritizes the integration of ECCE into the mainstream education system, ensuring access to quality pre-primary education for all children between the ages of 3 and 6.

3. Multilingualism:
- NEP 1986: The policy encouraged the use of the regional language as the medium of instruction up to the primary level, with a three-language formula (mother tongue, regional language, and English) implemented at the secondary level.
- NEP 2020: The policy puts greater emphasis on multilingualism, suggesting that children should be taught in their mother tongue or regional language up to at least Grade 5. The three-language formula is also more flexible, with states having the liberty to choose the third language.

4. Curriculum and Assessment Reforms:
- NEP 1986: The focus was largely on the traditional curriculum and rote learning, with high emphasis on board examinations.
- NEP 2020: The new policy emphasizes conceptual understanding, critical thinking, and experiential learning instead of rote memorization. It introduces competency-based assessment and continuous evaluation, aiming to minimize the importance of board examinations.

5. Vocational Education:
- NEP 1986: Vocational education was encouraged but not fully integrated into the curriculum.
- NEP 2020: Vocational education is given more prominence, with plans to integrate it into the school curriculum starting from Grade 6. This aims to develop skillsets and improve employability.

6. Higher Education:
- NEP 1986: The higher education system was regulated by various regulatory bodies and lacked flexibility in terms of curriculum and degree options.
- NEP 2020: NEP emphasizes a multidisciplinary approach, allowing students the flexibility to choose subjects across disciplines. It also establishes a single overarching regulatory body (the Higher Education Commission of India) for higher education institutions, except for law and medical colleges.

7. Technology in Education:
- NEP 1986: There was minimal emphasis on the use of technology in education.
- NEP 2020: The new policy recognizes the importance of technology and calls for a greater integration of technology into the education system, including the creation of a National Educational Technology Forum (NETF) to facilitate the use of technology in teaching and learning processes.

These changes and more within NEP 2020 demonstrate a commitment to improving access, equity, and quality in education, with a strong focus on skill development and preparing students for the challenges of the 21st century.</response>

[Question]A bowl of fruit holds 18 peaches. Four of the peaches are ripe and two more ripen every day, but on the third day three are eaten. How many more ripe peaches than unripe peaches are in the bowl after five days?

Problem:CONTEXT In patients with brain metastases, it is unclear whether adding up-front whole-brain radiation therapy (WBRT) to stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS) has beneficial effects on mortality or neurologic function compared with SRS alone.   
 OBJECTIVE To determine if WBRT combined with SRS results in improvements in survival, brain tumor control, functional preservation rate, and frequency of neurologic death.   
 DESIGN, SETTING, AND PATIENTS Randomized controlled trial of 132 patients with 1 to 4 brain metastases, each less than 3 cm in diameter, enrolled at 11 hospitals in Japan between October 1999 and December 2003.   
 INTERVENTIONS Patients were randomly assigned to receive WBRT plus SRS (65 patients) or SRS alone (67 patients).   
 MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES The primary end point was overall survival; secondary end points were brain tumor recurrence, salvage brain treatment, functional preservation, toxic effects of radiation, and cause of death.   
 RESULTS The median survival time and the 1-year actuarial survival rate were 7.5 months and 38.5% (95% confidence interval, 26.7%-50.3%) in the WBRT + SRS group and 8.0 months and 28.4% (95% confidence interval, 17.6%-39.2%) for SRS alone (P = .42). The 12-month brain tumor recurrence rate was 46.8% in the WBRT + SRS group and 76.4% for SRS alone group (P<.001). Salvage brain treatment was less frequently required in the WBRT + SRS group (n = 10) than with SRS alone (n = 29) (P<.001). Death was attributed to neurologic causes in 22.8% of patients in the WBRT + SRS group and in 19.3% of those treated with SRS alone (P = .64). There were no significant differences in systemic and neurologic functional preservation and toxic effects of radiation.   
 CONCLUSIONS Compared with SRS alone, the use of WBRT plus SRS did not improve survival for patients with 1 to 4 brain metastases, but intracranial relapse occurred considerably more frequently in those who did not receive WBRT. Consequently, salvage treatment is frequently required when up-front WBRT is not used.

6. Release or relocate the animal humanely: Once you've successfully trapped the animal, handle the cage with care. Wear gloves to protect both yourself and the animal. Release the animal in a suitable location, preferably away from human habitation and in its natural habitat.

2. Palacio de Bellas Artes - It's a beautiful cultural center and museum featuring murals by famous Mexican artists, such as Diego Rivera, as well as hosting world-class art exhibitions and performances.

3. Templo Mayor - Explore this Aztec archaeological site and its adjacent museum showcasing the impressive ruins of one of the Aztecs' most significant temples.

6. National Museum of Anthropology - This world-renowned museum showcases Mexico's rich and diverse history with artifacts from pre-Hispanic civilizations to the present day.

7. Coyoacán - Wander through this charming neighborhood known for its cobblestone streets, colorful houses, lively markets, and historic sites.

9. Teotihuacan - Take a day trip to the awe-inspiring ancient city of Teotihuacan. Climb the Pyramid of the Sun and Pyramid of the Moon for stunning views and a glimpse into Mexico's pre-Columbian history.

10. Paseo de la Reforma - Stroll down this famous avenue lined with modern skyscrapers, historical monuments, and beautiful green spaces. Don't miss the iconic Angel of Independence monument.

1. Data collection and preprocessing:
To begin with, data is collected from several sources such as GPS tracking collars, satellite imagery, climate data, and socio-economic information about local communities. Data preprocessing is then performed, involving cleaning, standardizing, and transforming the data to make it suitable for machine learning algorithms.

![Data Collection and Preprocessing](https://i.imgur.com/gHbt5GO.png)

2. Feature extraction:
Next, relevant features are identified and extracted from the preprocessed data. These features may include animal movement patterns, temperature patterns, ice cover, vegetation, available resources, and human activities such as hunting and fishing practices.

![Feature Extraction](https://i.imgur.com/qCVMFYn.png)

3. Model training and validation:
Machine learning algorithms are trained using the prepared dataset to predict animal migration patterns under different climate scenarios. These models are validated by comparing their predictions with historical migration routes and known animal behavior.

![Model Training and Validation](https://i.imgur.com/azP9O0L.png)

4. Analysis of climate change impact on migration:
Using the trained models, we can simulate various climate change scenarios and analyze the resulting changes in animal migration patterns. This can help us identify potential risks and challenges that might arise due to changed migration routes.

![Climate Change Impact](https://i.imgur.com/GbncjgM.png)

5. Impact assessment on local communities:
By integrating socio-economic data of local communities with the predicted changes in migration patterns, we can assess the potential impact on the livelihood, economy, food security, and cultural practices of these communities. This helps to identify the necessary adaptation measures to mitigate the risks.

![Impact Assessment](https://i.imgur.com/JATMMAy.png)

6. Communication and decision-making:
The results and insights generated by the machine learning models can be visualized and communicated to stakeholders, policymakers, and local communities, assisting them in making informed decisions regarding conservation efforts, resource management, and community adaptations to the changing environment.

![Communication and Decision-Making](https://i.imgur.com/tsM0Lqe.png)

In summary, machine learning algorithms can greatly contribute to understanding the complex relations between climate change, animal migration patterns, and the impact on local Arctic communities. By analyzing vast amounts of data and simulating various scenarios, these algorithms can help us make better-informed decisions and adapt to the ever-changing environment in the Arctic.</response>

<response>To create a shorter SQL query, you can use a lateral join to unnest the array of interests and then use a SELECT statement to get the interest id and name:
```sql
WITH interested_users AS (
  SELECT
    to_char(current_date, 'DD/MM/YYYY') AS date,
    fb_activity_offers.provider_activity_ref AS activity_id,
    jsonb_array_elements(targeting -> 'flexible_spec' -> 0 -> 'interests') AS interest
  FROM fb_template_adsets
  LEFT JOIN fb_template_campaigns ON fb_template_campaigns.id = fb_template_adsets.template_campaign_id
  LEFT JOIN fb_templates ON fb_templates.id = fb_template_campaigns.template_id
  LEFT JOIN fb_activity_offers ON fb_activity_offers.id = fb_templates.activity_offer_id
  WHERE offering_id = 'CLICKS'
)
SELECT
  date,
  activity_id,
  interest ->> 'id' AS interest_id,
  interest ->> 'name' AS interest_name
FROM interested_users
ORDER BY 1;
```
This query uses a common table expression (CTE) to perform the lateral join and unnest the interests array. Then, it selects the date, activity\_id, interest\_id, and interest\_name from the CTE and orders the result by the date.</response>

<response>To create a shorter SQL query, you can use a lateral join to unnest the array of interests and then use a SELECT statement to get the interest id and name:
```sql
WITH interested_users AS (
  SELECT
    to_char(current_date, 'DD/MM/YYYY') AS date,
    fb_activity_offers.provider_activity_ref AS activity_id,
    jsonb_array_elements(targeting -> 'flexible_spec' -> 0 -> 'interests') AS interest
  FROM fb_template_adsets
  LEFT JOIN fb_template_campaigns ON fb_template_campaigns.id = fb_template_adsets.template_campaign_id
  LEFT JOIN fb_templates ON fb_templates.id = fb_template_campaigns.template_id
  LEFT JOIN fb_activity_offers ON fb_activity_offers.id = fb_templates.activity_offer_id
  WHERE offering_id = 'CLICKS'
)
SELECT
  date,
  activity_id,
  interest ->> 'id' AS interest_id,
  interest ->> 'name' AS interest_name
FROM interested_users
ORDER BY 1;
```

Sub highlightCells()
    Dim rng As Range

```vbnet
Sub HighlightCells()

Dim ws As Worksheet
Set ws = ThisWorkbook.Worksheets("Sheet1")'replace "Sheet1" with the actual name of your sheet

With ws.Range("A1:G10")
   .FormatConditions.Delete
   .FormatConditions.Add xlCellValue, xlLessEqual, 0.1
   .FormatConditions(1).Interior.Color = vbYellow
End With

End Sub
```
This code creates a new format condition and sets its color to yellow for all cells in the range A1:G10 If their value is less than or equal to 0. You can change the color and the cell range as needed.</response>

<response>Title: Comprehensive Marketing Plan for NatureClean Natural Cleaning Products Launch

Introduction:
NatureClean is preparing to launch our new line of eco-friendly, non-toxic, and biodegradable cleaning products positioned to transform the way consumers approach cleanliness while considering environmental factors. This comprehensive marketing plan highlights each aspect of the launch strategy, ensuring alignment with the company’s mission and core values. 

1. Market Analysis:
To tailor our plan efficiently and provide products that cater to specific customer demands, we will examine current market trends, competitor analyses, challenges, and opportunities in the natural cleaning products sector. This will include understanding key players, their product offerings, price points, and market share, as well as analyzing consumer preferences, demands, and pain points.

2. Target Audience Identification:
Our target audience consists of environmentally conscious consumers who prioritize non-toxic, eco-friendly, and sustainable products. These customers span various age groups, primarily aged 25-54, seeking natural alternatives to chemical solutions. Identifying and segmenting this audience will help us create focused messaging and positioning for our products.

3. Product Positioning:
NatureClean's product positioning is built upon the unique selling propositions (USPs) of our natural cleaning products. These USPs include:

- Non-toxic and plant-based ingredients
- Biodegradable packaging
- Cruelty-free and vegan
- Energy and water-efficient production methods
- Superior efficacy compared to traditional cleaning products

4. Branding Guidelines:
To communicate our brand ethos effectively, we will develop a set of clear branding guidelines, including logo usage, font styles, color schemes, and messaging tone. These guidelines will create a consistent and easily recognizable identity for NatureClean's products across all marketing channels.

5. Social Media Tactics:
We will harness the power of social media – Instagram, Facebook, Twitter, Pinterest, and LinkedIn – to reach and engage our audience. Tactics will include content marketing, user-generated stories, influencer collaborations, social listening, and community engagement. Social media will enable us to showcase our values, share educational resources, and foster meaningful relationships with consumers.

6. Advertising Budget:
The advertising budget will be strategically allocated across digital platforms such as Google Ads, social media advertising, sponsored content, and targeted email campaigns, as well as traditional marketing channels such as print advertising, radio, and TV ads. To optimize our budget, we will track ROI and continually adjust ad spend across different channels.

7. Promotional Strategies:
To generate initial buzz and create long-term customer loyalty, we will utilize various promotional strategies, including:

- A launch event with influencer partnerships
- Introductory discounts and product bundles
- Loyalty programs and referral schemes
- Collaborations with eco-friendly organizations and events
- Sampling programs at local stores and events

8. Sales Forecasts:
Our sales forecasts will be based on historical data, market research, and consumer trends. We will establish realistic short-term and long-term sales goals, identifying opportunities and risks based on seasonal variations, promotional efforts, and potential market shifts.

9. Goals, Timelines, and KPIs:
To measure the success of our marketing plan, we will set Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, and Time-bound (SMART) goals. Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) will include metrics such as website traffic, social media engagement, cost per acquisition, conversion rates, and total sales. Timelines for reaching these goals will be established to maintain focus and motivation throughout the launch process.

Conclusion:
NatureClean's comprehensive marketing plan will ensure a successful product launch by understanding our market, audience, and value proposition, while executing strategies in line with the company's core values and mission. Through regular monitoring and data analysis, we will optimize our efforts, making necessary adjustments to sustain growth and maximize the impact of our natural cleaning products.</response>

Problem:[[-97, -53, 54, 84, 35], [65, 87, -95, -76, -94, 22, 38, 55], [-90, 48, 59, -58, 26, 37], [-61, -23], [68, 64]]
Solution:
<response>To solve this problem, follow these steps:

1. Identify the length of the longest inner list. This will help you determine the length of the final output list.
2. Create an empty list called `output` to store the summed values.
3. Iterate through the inner lists using a for loop.
4. Inside the loop, calculate the sum of the values at each position of the current inner list.
5. Append the calculated sum to the `output` list.
6. After the loop, check if the length of the `output` list is equal to the length of the shortest inner list. If not, fill the missing values with zeros using another for loop. This ensures that the output list is the same length as the longest inner list.
7. Return the `output` list as the solution.

Let's apply these steps to the given problem:

```python
# Problem: [[-97, -53, 54, 84, 35], [65, 87, -95, -76, -94, 22, 38, 55], [-90, 48, 59, -58, 26, 37], [-61, -23], [68, 64]]

# Step 1: Identify the length of the longest inner list

# Step 2: Create an empty list called `output`

    output.append(inner_sum)

# Step 6: Fill the missing values with zeros
for i in range(max_length):
    if i >= len(output):
        output.append(0)

# Step 7: Return the `output` list as the solution
solution = output
print(solution)
```

```
[106, 144, -23, -50, 45, 80]
```

This is the correct solution to the given problem.</response>

User: Instructions: Write a question from the passage such that it identifies a character (a person or a thing) in the passage.
Input: I was fencing wire at Flat Broke Acres and trying to tighten up the wire a bit. I lost the grip of the fencing wire and the pliers smacked me in the mouth.
This is what I hit myself in the mouth with. The curved end glance off my left front central incisor.
It hurt some, my lips were lacerated, I scared my wife when I came in to take a look at it in the mirror but the pain to come was far worse. Tooth was intact thank goodness and was a bit wobbly and I said to myself yup, this could be a problem. A month or two later I hit it again when I was putting a portable step fence panel in the bed of the truck and it bounced and split the bridge of my nose and hit the tooth again. did not break or get displaced. Thank goodness I have a particularly thick head.
Tooth trauma is a strange thing. It can blow up anywhere up to a year later. So almost 6 months later I was flying to a meeting in Orlando and of course the tooth decided to react to changes in atmospheric pressure just so I could experience the exquisite pain of barodontalgia. Kind of pain that makes you want to pry the top of your head off with a pitchfork because it would take your mind off the pain.
Problem was it did not resolve after landing or anytime during the 4 days I was at the meeting. A combo regimen of acetaminophen and ibuprofen manage the pain well enough until I could get home and have it seen to. Pain did not end but the Xray showed no fracture or endodontic lesion. Strange. Then as suddenly as it occurred, the pain ceased. Strange x 2. Snapped another film and there was no pathology. Tooth was vital on pulp testing. So I did nothing more.
I chalked it up to it being a karmic reminder about patients and dental pain as I've never had a cavity let alone a dental abscess. It let me feel your pain.
Output:
<response>What object did the person accidentally hit their mouth with while fencing wire at Flat Broke Acres?</response>

answer:
